records.verified_title: HG-Adapter: Improving Pre-Trained Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks with Dual Adapters
records.publication_status: arXiv v1; later venue not verified in this bounded lane
exact_read_scope: Sections2.1-2.4: typed graph definition, dual low-rank structure adapters, relation weights, label propagation and objectives; theorem statements read, proofs not audited
AppendixB algorithm; adjacent proof beginning was visible, no proof audit
AppendixD.3-D.5 downstream protocol, architecture and computing-resource claims
paper_evidence: Section2.3 Eq4 factorizes adapter W_delta=W_down W_up before ReLU; W_vartheta for same-type structure similarity is also decomposed into low-rank matrices.
Same-type homogeneous structure is a positive symmetrized k-nearest-neighbor similarity graph; adapter output A F is added to frozen post-message embeddings.
Section2.3 Eq8-10 uses another low-rank adapter and a per-target-node softmax across neighbor/relation types; its weighted neighbor representation is added to frozen heterogeneous embeddings.
Section2.4 uses training-label propagation A Y, class-subgraph contrast, feature reconstruction and a margin objective. AppendixD.3 evaluates probabilities from similarity to class-subgraph vectors.
Algorithm initializes/uploads pretraining, then tunes adapters/projection. Exact factor initialization, k, rank and initial learning-rate value are not fixed by the selected implementation paragraph.
records.saved_takeaway: Low-rank graph adaptation with typed structural weighting and label-informed optimization is direct prior. It is not a BatchEnsemble committee or proof of an exact node/relation-indexed rank-one ensemble.
records.candidate_relationship: Defeats novelty based on adding heterogeneity, compact adapters, task-related relation weighting or supervised graph structure alone. It adds member-specific structural propagation work if turned into an ensemble.
limitations: No author-linked implementation URL found in the retained paper HTML; exact implementation not retrieved.
The generalization theorem statements were read for method context; their proof, pseudo-label-as-extra-sample assumptions and graph-dependence conditions were not independently validated.
Published/runtime figures are source claims, not current-project resource measurements.

records.verified_title: Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Relational Deep Learning
records.publication_status: New arXiv v1 preprint; no acceptance or independent reproduction asserted
exact_read_scope: Full main method3.1-3.2 and setup4.1: temporal features, relation maps, objectives, budget and chronological evaluation
AppendixA task/database sizes and splits; B.1 validation family selection and baseline table
AppendicesC-D: full architecture/optimizer/budget/temporal encoding recipe and endpoint-adapter interaction
paper_evidence: TimeMix shares learned temporal scales/mixture weights but uses table-specific projection g_(a,k). AppendixD initializes scales at1s,1min,1h,1day and mixture logits equally.

TimeRoPE rotates source/target features in GNN messages; each relation has W_neigh^(r) and W_self^(r), then relation outputs are summed. THGFM uses relation-specific attention and a shared-space branch with endpoint adapters and type-conditioned gated fusion.

Temp-Sub uses typed mean pooling followed by type-specific learned projections and shared attention; relation-preserving edge dropout retains reverse edges jointly and at least one edge per represented relation.
Historical relation recovery uses a relation-specific bilinear decoder and removes the positive target edge and reverse from inputs; future relation activity uses cutoff-constrained horizon labels.
Five RelBench databases and11tasks use original chronological splits; four seeds42-45. HeteroGNN and THGFM were selected among five baselines using mean validation rank, not test performance.

Native recipe:3graph layers,width128; GT8heads;4-layer table ResNets; fanouts128/64/32; AdamW lr0.002 wd1e-5;100k pretraining and100k downstream steps; full encoder fine-tuning; task-metric validation checkpoint selection.
Best evaluated staged schedules depend on backbone and encodings; gains are not uniform across task types.
records.saved_takeaway: A very recent heterogeneous predictive framework provides competent typed/temporal baselines and chronological evaluation. Type-specific maps, relation transforms, typed pooling, endpoint adapters and structural initialization/pretraining already coexist. It does not demonstrate a rank-one ensemble or its uncertainty benefit.
records.candidate_relationship: A heterogeneous GNNM claim must earn predictive/calibration utility and charge all pretraining plus complete private graph trajectories against this recent baseline. Sharing matrices alone cannot inherit temporal/type specialization as novelty or compute savings.
limitations: Author code or dataset exports were not fetched. Exact endpoint-adapter parameterization is unspecified by the scoped passage, so rank-one equivalence with this backbone is not claimed.
Native recipe is a reference, not an admitted reproducible runtime. Text feature preparation, graph building and temporal sampling are material costs.
Data/split values are paper metadata, not verified local dataset artifacts.
